posts.cooked:
Fun and easy Mint. :) Shut up, little man.

If anyone needs pointers, I'll just say this: flog those Grease Guns! Mr. Fixer ain't got much else to do, and I got to use them a total of four times. Keeping Mainstay's environment destruction card from the start is also a good idea for when the paparazzi show up.

posts.name: starkenburg_alexander
posts.cooked:
Mint-Flavored Grease Brawl?

Fun little one shot, with no thought for defense from either side ended with 3/7/7/2. I could have played much more conservative, but where is the fun in that?

I am pretty sure between the 4 grease guns, the heroes did more damage to themselves than the villains did, what with Hermetic and Fright Train's incap ability. Setback was the ongoing handler, Mr. Fixer liberally sprayed the villains, Mainstay was a danger to himself and others, and Haka.... just kinda punched people?

I am also sure Haka would not appreciate Guise calling his mere a maraca, though he would kindly explain the difference to Guise after the fight, showing how it is a time honored weapon of his people (and not by bashing Guise on the head with it, Haka wouldn't do that).

~Komori

posts.name: bolnerap
posts.cooked: Curbstomping on my end, final HP 13 / 18 / 15 / 14. Only needed two Grease Guns. Probably would have gone more quickly if I hadn't played Fumbling Fool to take advantage of the two Exceeded Expectations in the opening hand, but eh. I popped Proletariat, Fright Train, and Bugbear very quickly, but the Operative hung around for a couple rounds because Megalopolis is Megalopolis and it temporarily slowed me down.

posts.name: Missingno
posts.cooked: Mint at 7/11/6/4.  Four grease guns really removes the threat from this fight, JUST!  PUMMEL!  BUGBEAR!  FIRST!  He pulls out Feral Brawn pretty early, so you really don't want to stall him out for too long.  Had an amusing Whops, Sorry! moment with Setback blowing up Fixer's Bloody Knuckles on the turn where he didn't have Salvage Yard in hand to spare the guy some HP.
